correctness.rationale: Exact categorical enumeration gives all three coefficients. A discriminant inequality for up to five categories follows for every real probability vector via the sharp five-coordinate cubic extremal inequality, strict monotonicity of the discriminant in the third power sum and the positive factored one-heavy family. An exact six-category rational example has discriminant -1439/810000. The complete analytic proof includes boundaries; standalone code checks exact identities and examples.

evidence: O'Neill Theorem 1 and Section 7 explicitly use independent uniform bin indices; Sections 2–8 concern uniform occupancy, spillage and hitting times.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Uniform occupancy results are on a narrower categorical-parent subclass, while generic negative-association conclusions do not force real-rootedness of the three-draw richness PGF. Neither subsumes the five-category threshold.

evidence: O'Neill gives uniform-bin occupancy formulas; Tang–Tang gives general polynomial characterization without evaluating this nonuniform occupancy family.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Combining these results establishes neither the universal bound on the discriminant for unequal five-point masses nor the explicit six-category violation without the new five-coordinate extremal argument.

evidence: Tang–Tang identifies real-rootedness, Pólya-frequency and independent-Bernoulli convolution as equivalent notions; it does not assert a universal five-category three-draw occupancy case.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The claim was compared both as a coefficient discriminant assertion, as two-Bernoulli decomposability, and as real-zero property. General equivalence translates the question but does not resolve its sharp parameter threshold.

evidence: The six-point discriminant is derived directly from a rational probability vector; no precomputed occupancy table or fixed-parameter database was used.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The statement is uniform over all continuous parameters for up to five labels; a finite table would not alone imply it. No matching exact three-draw classification table was identified.

originality.rationale: Theorem 4.1 in Tang–Tang establishes the characterization of real-rooted PGFs but contains no three-draw categorical richness threshold. O'Neill treats uniform box allocation, not arbitrary weights; the accessible descriptions of related exposed-point and covariance research address distinct properties. No identical or stronger coverage was located. Residual risk: unindexed classical inequality may imply the sharp bound.
residual_risks: Older unindexed occupancy, discrete probability, or symmetric-polynomial work may already imply this exact sharp support threshold.
Some mathematical-record search requests were transiently unavailable; those failed requests were not counted as successful database comparisons.

value.rationale: Provides a sharp, natural and complete support-size cutoff for a distributional representation of three-draw species richness. Both the all-probability positive classification and a strict six-category obstruction are required; the result is not a mere example or computational table.
